minutes.headline: Zoning board approved a larger ground-mount solar array at 63 Pratt St and a five-unit shopping center at 88 Mass Ave.
minutes.summary: The remote Zoning Board of Appeals heard two special permit petitions. It granted a modification adding five panels to a previously approved ground-mount solar system, and a special permit to divide 88 Massachusetts Avenue into five tenant spaces, subject to planning board review. The board then went into executive session on pending litigation.

votes.motion: Grant approval of the increase in the solar array by five panels at 63 Pratt Street, in the same location, closer to the house, per the earlier special permit.
Grant a special permit at 88 Mass Ave changing three tenant spaces to five, subject to planning board review.
Enter executive session to discuss litigation strategy, then adjourn afterward.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit to change 88 Mass Ave from three tenant spaces to five, subject to planning board review.
The board approved a modification to a previously approved ground-mount solar array at 63 Pratt Street, adding five panels in the same location, closer to the house.
The vote counts on both petitions were not audible in the captions; the chair stated the outcomes, with standard post-decision conditions.
The applicant at 88 Mass Ave said parking lot paving was paused until approval, and that the owners carry a mortgage and want to rent smaller spaces.
The board then voted to enter executive session on litigation.

why_it_matters: The 88 Mass Ave permit allows more, smaller tenant spaces on one commercial property, which can change traffic, parking and neighborhood use once the planning board completes its review.
The solar change is a small increase to an already permitted home system, so it adds no new location or use for neighbors.
watch_next: Planning board review of the 88 Mass Ave division into five tenant spaces, which the special permit depends on.
